title: fix(slack): read a mention's blocks and attachments, not only its text
body:
## Problem

A customer tags the PostHog app, and the words of their request never reach the agent. Two shapes:

- The words live in the message's `blocks` or `attachments`, not its `text`. `event["text"]` reads none of them, so a mention sent by a Slack workflow or a rich-text client arrives empty.
- The message has no text of its own, only an attachment. The one record of the request is that message inside the context block, but the block's header and annotations point the agent *past* it, to the prompt slot below the closing tag, which holds only the fallback title.

In both, `_build_posthog_code_task_description` returns its fallback and the agent opens with "I don't see a request in this thread".

## Changes

- A mention whose words are in `blocks` or `attachments` now reaches the agent. The activity reads the event through `extract_message_text`, which merges `text`, `blocks`, and `attachments`, the same extractor the thread and fork paths already use. `event["text"]` was the only path still reading one source.
- A mention with no text of its own keeps its message in the context block. The placeholder that stands in for the initiator's message is used only when the prompt below the divider actually repeats it; with no prompt, the message and its attachment stay in the block instead of being replaced and dropped.
- The block's header, the role annotation, and the request line now point *inside* the tag when there is no initiator text, so the agent reads the message and its file as the ask rather than skipping to the placeholder title.
- No change when the mention has text, which is the overwhelming majority.

Out of scope: a mention that is only `@PostHog` with nothing else still resolves to the fallback, because there is genuinely no request to recover. Answering that case without a sandbox run is a separate follow-up, gated on the untagged-reply routing that keeps a thread live.

## How did you test this code?

- `hogli test posthog/temporal/tests/ai/slack_app/activities/test_task_creation.py` — 41 pass, including the existing case that asserts a genuinely empty thread still returns the bare fallback.
- New unit case: with no initiator text and a screenshot as the whole message, the description must not equal the fallback, must not contain the placeholder, and must keep the attachment note.
- The activity-boundary extraction is covered in `products/slack_app/backend/tests/test_followup_forwarding.py` with a mention whose words live only in `blocks`.
- Not measured: how many of the affected turns this recovers. A sample showed most were bare `@PostHog` mentions, which stay out of scope above.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5 (1M context), plus a PostHog Desktop task run that added the context-header commit on the same branch.

The finding came from reading Slack app traces where the agent's whole user message was the literal string `Task from Slack`. The first commit reads `blocks`/`attachments` and guards the placeholder; a PostHog Desktop task then added the commit that repoints the header and annotations at the in-tag message. This description covers the combined diff.

Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`.

CodeRabbit CLI pass: skipped, signed out. `auto_review` posts on open.

No customer data or session content is in this branch. The counts that motivated the fix come from PostHog's own AI observability data.
